reasons.rubric: Non-membership bit is simple and high-frequency-ish, but the moment is a niche, questionable screen with a legally doubtful verifier demand, so it is a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Operators rarely screen enforcement-debtor status, the idea admits it may be unlawful, and non-membership does not prove ability to pay.
reasons.coherence: The stated goal of assuring payment capacity does not match the predicate, which proves only absence from a register.
reasons.novelty: Court-register non-membership for childcare is a new moment, though close in spirit to the known landlord clean-record case.
reasons.provenance: The voting-ballot separation borrowing is decorative; the idea reads the same without it and the mechanism is unrelated.
reasons.retention_law: A private operator has no obvious duty to retain the full file, though the legal propriety of the check itself is doubtful.
reasons.linkability: A single non-membership attestation is a stable per-person value unless made unlinkable, and the operator already holds the ID copy.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Courts are unlikely to sign attestations to support a questionable private screen of parents.
reasons.no_wallet: Parents and small operators would need a wallet, and the ID copy is still collected, so the benefit is largely lost.

reasons.rubric: A class-membership predicate from an existing utility issuer is simple, but grants are infrequent and the bureau also needs the address and a site visit.
reasons.validity: The grant moment is real, but the bureau needs the site address for the project record, so class membership alone is not sufficient for the final decision.
reasons.coherence: The over-collection problem and the narrow membership claim fit together, with the idea itself admitting the limit at final approval.
reasons.novelty: Electricity-contract class for agricultural grants is a moment not on the known list, though close to the utility-subsidy case.
reasons.provenance: The borrowing about narrowing a bundled request to a single claim does shape the framing, but the idea would read much the same without the age-flag analogy.
reasons.retention_law: A government grant file likely needs the site address and supporting records retained, so ZK reduces exposure only at the application stage.
reasons.linkability: Membership without account number is hard to deduplicate or audit, and the later address disclosure links the applicant anyway.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Taipower is a state-owned utility and could plausibly sign class membership, but it has little incentive to build this.
reasons.no_wallet: Farmers would need a wallet, and the county office can obtain the bills through ordinary channels, so adoption is doubtful.

reasons.rubric: The predicate is a time-bounded clearance, but outbreaks are episodic so frequency is low and the issuer ecosystem needs hospitals to participate.
reasons.validity: Outbreak-window clearance is a real situation, but a facility may be entitled to more in an active case and hospitals rarely issue such clearances.
reasons.coherence: The minimal clearance, validity window and sensitivity of the underlying report fit together well.
reasons.novelty: Infectious-disease clearance for communal housing is a moment nobody on the known list touches.
reasons.retention_law: Communicable-disease rules may let the facility or authorities require fuller records in an active case; I cannot say.
reasons.linkability: A signed clearance with an expiry is a bearer value that could be correlated if presented repeatedly across facilities.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals are cautious about issuing portable health attestations and may refuse to create new credentials.
reasons.no_wallet: Migrant workers and students may lack a compatible wallet, and public health reporting may bypass self-presented proof.

reasons.rubric: A uniqueness nullifier on a high-frequency promo moment has a real over-collection problem, but the carrier ecosystem is fragmented and one-per-person is hard to issue, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Promotion draws are real and phone-number farming is a real problem, but a per-line telco credential does not prove one person per entry and winners must give ID anyway.
reasons.coherence: The nullifier fits the one-entry goal, though the idea itself notes that SIM rules allow several lines per person, which undermines the uniqueness claim.
reasons.novelty: Promotion draws are not on the known list; the nullifier resembles the known brokerage Sybil case but the moment and issuer are new.
reasons.provenance: The SameSite cookie and census disclosure-limitation borrowings are decorative; a campaign-scoped nullifier follows from the one-entry goal without them.
reasons.retention_law: Retailers have no apparent duty to keep phone numbers, though winners' tax withholding forces identity collection at the prize stage.
reasons.linkability: Campaign-scoped tags avoid cross-campaign linkage by design, though the carrier could see which campaigns are entered if it participates in proofs.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Carriers would need to issue a per-person rather than per-line credential, which the idea itself says they may not do.
reasons.no_wallet: Casual entrants will not install a wallet for a convenience-store draw when an SMS code is easy, so friction likely kills adoption.

reasons.rubric: A non-membership bit is simple, but the program separately requires positive income and property checks, so only a small part of the file is removed and frequency is low.
reasons.validity: The moment is plausible, but the operator may query the government list directly, and non-blacklisting is insufficient for the eligibility decision.
reasons.coherence: The framing of a landlord collecting full transcripts conflicts with a predicate that covers only the blacklist part of the check.
reasons.novelty: Subsidy-program disqualification lists are a new predicate, but the moment overlaps the known rental and subsidy cases.
reasons.provenance: The bank account-opening borrowing is decorative, since it describes unspecified retention and nothing in the idea depends on it.
reasons.retention_law: A subsidy program likely needs the full eligibility file retained for audit, so ZK would reduce exposure in transit only.
reasons.linkability: A non-membership claim to a single operator carries little extra linkage beyond the identity the operator already holds.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: A housing agency could sign a list check, but it can also simply offer a direct lookup to the operator, which removes the need.
reasons.no_wallet: Tenants would need a wallet while the operator still collects the other records, so the practical benefit is small.

reasons.rubric: A roll membership bit is simple with a plausible issuer, but the roll is derived from local welfare data, so the issuer is fragmented and frequency is low.
reasons.validity: Community energy schemes do ask for bills, but the bill is not the natural proof and Taipower may not hold the welfare roll.
reasons.coherence: The scheme need, the bill over-disclosure and the nullifier fit, but the issuer is uncertain and nearly duplicates the sibling grant idea.
reasons.novelty: It is a reworded utility-subsidy case already known, applied to a solar co-op, so novelty is low.
reasons.provenance: Both borrowings only restate that the proof should carry just the membership bit; the idea would read the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: A small township or NGO programme probably has no legal duty to keep the full bill, though audit rules for public funds are unknown.
reasons.linkability: The nullifier is deliberate to prevent double claims, which makes the account linkable within the scheme but not obviously across schemes.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Taipower is not the owner of welfare status and the welfare bureaus would have to sign instead, so the named issuer may decline.
reasons.no_wallet: Low-income households and small NGO counters may lack wallets or readers, and a photocopy is easy.

reasons.rubric: A non-membership bit on a ban list from a government issuer is simple and the full certificate over-discloses, but a legally defined certificate form and freshness issues limit it.
reasons.validity: Checking people who work with children is a real duty in Taiwan, but the legal check may be defined as a specific certificate, so the proof may not satisfy it.
reasons.coherence: The over-disclosing certificate, the narrower ban-list claim and the freshness caveat fit together well.
reasons.novelty: It is close to the known clean-criminal-record rental case but applies to a different verifier and a narrower register.
reasons.retention_law: Organisations may be required to keep the prescribed certificate, which I cannot confirm, and that could remove the benefit.
reasons.linkability: A stable non-membership attestation could be correlated across organisations unless presentations are unlinkable.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Several ministries would have to cooperate on a combined register, and a justice-derived record is sensitive to sign.
reasons.no_wallet: Volunteers at temples and clubs are often older or non-technical and small groups lack verifier tooling.

reasons.rubric: A date-range attestation is simple and high-frequency with a trusted issuer, but the predicate needs only two fields, and employers may insist on the diagnosis certificate.
reasons.validity: Sick-leave proof is a very real moment, and the date range is enough for leave approval, but a hospital would need to issue a new document type.
reasons.coherence: The minimal attestation, the sensitivity of diagnoses and the adoption caveat fit together well.
reasons.novelty: Medical leave proof for employers is not on the known list, though it resembles a health-disclosure moment in general.
reasons.retention_law: Employers may be required to keep leave records and some contracts or insurers demand the diagnosis, which I cannot confirm.
reasons.linkability: A date-range attestation reveals only hospitalisation timing and is presented to one employer, so cross-context linkage is minor.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals already issue certificates and could issue a diagnosis-free version, though they may be reluctant to change workflow.
reasons.no_wallet: Employees can simply be given a diagnosis-free paper certificate, so no wallet is needed and ZK adds little.
